reply_text:
I found no dated AI prediction from Mark Zuckerberg in 2013. I ran the three required searches as written and four more of my own (seven of 12), and used all six page openings.

**What 2013 held:**
- **Earnings call, 30 October 2013.** Zuckerberg said Facebook had formed an AI group in September to help make sense of what people share. VentureBeat reprints part of what he said there, ending with: "Over time, I think it's going to be possible to build services that are much more natural to interact with and can help solve many more problems than any existing technology today." I left this out because "over time" gives no date and the line isn't about when AGI arrives. I saw these words only in VentureBeat's article. The full call transcript wouldn't load at Seeking Alpha (it cut off after the opening remarks) or as the Marquette University PDF.
- **NIPS conference, December 2013.** He took part in a panel at the deep learning workshop. The only account I opened is a Hacker News user's bullet-point summary. It says he described a "long-time vision" of AI as an "exo-cortex," but it isn't his own words and gives no date. A commenter there also asks whether he actually used that word. I didn't find a recording or transcript.

**Other years:** The 29 January 2014 earnings call is where he gave his three-, five- and ten-year plan, including "five years from now" AI forecasts. That belongs to 2014. Nothing from 2013 was already recorded.

**Gaps:** I didn't open the Atlantic Live interview (18 September 2013), the Wired Q&A (April 2013) or the 24 July 2013 earnings call transcript. The Marquette "Zuckerberg Files" archive lists the first two. Nothing I saw suggested they contain AI forecasts, but I can't rule it out.
